installation.note: clear is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: clear clears the terminal screen by scrolling content up. It doesn't actually delete content - you can still scroll up to see previous output. It's equivalent to pressing Ctrl+L in most terminals. Use it to clean up your terminal display when it gets cluttered.

syntax.description: Clear the terminal screen. No options or arguments required.

examples.title: Clear terminal
examples.output: (screen is cleared, cursor moves to top)

elements.meaning: Previous output is scrolled up and hidden

breakdown.scroll: Previous content can still be scrolled up to view
breakdown.note: Content isn't deleted, just hidden - you can scroll up to see it

output_explanation.notes: clear doesn't actually delete content - it just scrolls it up. You can still scroll up to see previous output in most terminals.

examples.use_case: Quickly clear terminal to start fresh

examples.title: Clear and run command

output_explanation.format: Screen cleared then command output shown

elements.meaning: Clear screen, then if successful (&&), run ls

breakdown.&&: Logical AND - runs ls only if clear succeeds
breakdown.useful: Start fresh before running a command

output_explanation.notes: Common pattern to clear screen before running a command. The && ensures ls only runs if clear succeeds.

examples.use_case: Clear terminal before running a command for clean output

misconceptions.title: clear deletes content
misconceptions.reality: clear just scrolls content up - you can still scroll up to see previous output in most terminals. It doesn't actually delete anything.
misconceptions.tip: clear = hide content, not delete it. You can usually scroll up to see previous output. Use reset for true reset (harder to recover).

misconceptions.title: Ctrl+L is different from clear
misconceptions.misconception: Ctrl+L does something different than clear command
misconceptions.reality: Ctrl+L and clear do the same thing in most terminals. Ctrl+L is just a keyboard shortcut for clear.
misconceptions.tip: Ctrl+L = clear command. Both do the same thing - clear the screen.

common_pitfalls.description: Thinking previous output is gone after clear
common_pitfalls.solution: Remember that clear just hides content - you can usually scroll up in terminal to see previous output. Content isn't deleted.

common_pitfalls.description: Mixing up clear and reset commands
common_pitfalls.solution: clear just clears screen. reset also resets terminal settings and colors - use only if terminal is corrupted.

related_commands.relationship: Terminal reset; clear hides, reset resets terminal
related_commands.description: Reset terminal (more drastic than clear - resets terminal settings)

best_practices: Use clear or Ctrl+L to clean up terminal display
Use clear && command to start fresh before running commands
Remember previous output can still be scrolled up to view
Use reset only if terminal is corrupted or has display issues
performance_tips: clear is instant - very fast command
No performance impact - just display manipulation

additional_notes.keyboard_shortcut: Ctrl+L does the same as clear command in most terminals
additional_notes.content_preserved: clear doesn't delete content - it just scrolls it up. Previous output can still be viewed by scrolling up.
additional_notes.vs_reset: clear = just hide output. reset = reset terminal settings (more drastic, use if terminal corrupted)
additional_notes.common_pattern: clear && command is common pattern to start fresh before running a command
